title: This entire game was 100% generated by Gemini. The era of vibe game dev has arrived.
author: uskyeeeee

comments.author: uskyeeeee
comments.body: When my Reddit followers hit the triple digits (100+), this project is going open-source on AI Studio! Consider that a little digital bribe. 😉

comments.author: Brave-History-6502
comments.body: This isn't a game -- more like a POC

comments.author: imnotabot303
comments.body:
You mean the era of people who don't know how to make games, don't know how to code, don't know how to make audio and don't know how to make art, making trash games.

I don't understand the fascination in this sub with people constantly making posts like this. It's basically people boasting about how little input and effort they have put into something.

replies.author: uskyeeeee
replies.body:
Not knowing how to code, how to make audio, or how to create art doesn't mean you can't make a good game. Sure, lowering the barrier to entry will produce a lot of trash, but it will also raise the overall ceiling. The ones who should be worried are those who can only make audio, only make art, or only code—yet have mediocre game design talent.
This project is something I put together today while slacking off at work. I completed my normal tasks and still produced a demo. So many people who want to make games are trapped in their day jobs. My friend took out a loan to make a game and ultimately failed. The cost of game development is too high, and it shouldn't be this way.

replies.author: imnotabot303
replies.body: It's not because game development cost is too high. It's the opposite, there's an abundance of cheap or free software, assets and tutorials. It's never been easier or cheaper to make a game. The reason is just  because creating good games is difficult, a lot more difficult than people realise. 99.9% of everyone that tries to make a game without experience or skills in any of those areas will fail.

replies.author: emacrema
replies.body:
In my opinion, the market will still award good games made with love and care.. the world has always been full of copycats and low-value "stuff" ... this tech is lowering the barrier of entry for many people.. which doesn't necessarily mean that people won't pour their heart into it

I could argue that the real risk is that many people will need to reinvent themselves, as they will no longer be needed for their hard skills.. this is just my opinion.. let's talk about it

replies.author: imnotabot303
replies.body:
I agree. I'm not against using AI for game dev. AI is an amazing tool. What I have a problem with is the people that think demonstrating how little input they have had is somehow a good thing. 

There's a big difference between people using it as a tool and people saying hey Gemini make me a game.

comments.author: godver3
comments.body: So I agree and I don't - this is a proof of concept, not a game. Additionally I don't believe that Gemini (or other LLMs) can scale to full games - they can produce short piece like this, but we aren't yet to the point of scaling beyond this (with minor examples). I think we are getting closer though.

replies.author: Gone2MyMetalhead
replies.body:
I think we’ll get there but agree it’s no where near what people hope it is today. LLMs have strong limitations in anything spatial. Can you hand it a JSON or other data structure and say “move this +2m in X”? Sure — but I’d argue that’s a pretty terrible regression over modern tooling. Understanding why things go where they do and composability, not even get into the concept of non-language/image prompting, is in its infancy (and aren’t LLMs). 

If vibing game dev is just the programming part? Yeah LLMs are doing a lot. Asset Gen has come a long way even just this year, but still isn’t ready for production without a lot of manual clean up. And then there’s the rest of the pipeline….

replies.author: uskyeeeee
replies.body:
The voxel model in this game was also generated by Gemini, and Gemini's breakthrough lies in the fact that it truly possesses spatial and artistic capabilities. I can deeply feel this when I use it for drawing. The reason I use voxels is that voxels are essentially code; Gemini sees the code and immediately knows what the model is and what it looks like, which is not comparable to ordinary meshes.
It can also handle scene design on its own (though it is currently still quite crude), and it can split voxels to create animations.
Of course, my title is an exaggeration. The current problem with AI is still hallucination, which means I need to guide the AI to implement a reasonable architecture and module design. This remains difficult for people without programming experience.
I personally believe that if the hallucination problem is solved, then people won't even need to make games anymore, because AI will design them better than everyone else. Therefore, this very moment is the age of 'vibe gaming dev.'

comments.body: Cool but.... Can't say I'm thrilled about the already over saturated indie game market getting sprayed with a fire hose of Ai slop.
